input: Build a capsule travel toiletry bag for carry-on

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The exact categories of products to include (skincare, haircare, oral care, medicine, grooming) determine how many items and how much space is needed.
Whether this is for one person or shared with a partner/family changes the quantity and variety of products required.
The type and length of trip (e.g., 2-day business trip vs. 2-week vacation) dictates how minimal or comprehensive the kit needs to be.
A strict budget affects whether to invest in reusable travel bottles, branded travel-size products, or repurpose what is already owned.
Personal priorities — such as skincare routine complexity or hair type — heavily influence which products are non-negotiable vs. skippable.
Knowing whether the goal is a one-time packing list or a permanent ready-to-go bag that stays packed changes how the kit is built and maintained.
Whether the user already has a bag and travel-size containers, or needs to buy everything from scratch, determines the immediate first action.

gold.taskTitle: Build a carry-on capsule travel toiletry bag
gold.taskDescription: Curate a compact, TSA-compliant toiletry bag with only the essentials needed for carry-on travel.

questions.title: Which product categories must be in the bag?
questions.description: Identify which categories are non-negotiable: skincare, haircare, oral care, shaving/grooming, feminine hygiene, first aid, or other.

questions.title: Who is this toiletry bag packed for?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is a solo kit or needs to cover multiple people, such as a partner or children.

questions.title: What is the typical trip length and type?
questions.description: Determine whether this kit is built for short weekend trips, week-long vacations, or open-ended travel, and whether trips are business or leisure.

questions.title: What is your budget for building this kit?
questions.description: Establish whether the user wants to spend under $20, $20–$50, or more, which affects the bag, bottles, and product choices.

questions.title: Are there any products you refuse to downsize or skip?
questions.description: Identify personal non-negotiables — such as a specific moisturizer, prescription medication, or styling product — that must be accommodated.

questions.title: Should this bag stay permanently packed between trips?
questions.description: Clarify whether the goal is a dedicated always-ready travel kit or a packing checklist to assemble before each trip.

questions.title: Do you already have a bag and travel-size containers?
questions.description: Find out what the user is starting with — existing quart bag, dedicated toiletry case, reusable bottles — to determine what still needs to be sourced.
